"'''I Wanna Know'''" is a song by American [[contemporary R&B|R&B]] singer [[Joe (singer)|Joe]]. It was written by Joe, Joylon Skinner and Michele Williams for his third studio album ''[[My Name Is Joe (album)|My Name Is Joe]]'', which was released on April 18, 2000,<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4w4EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA27|page=27|title=Rhythm Section |last=Lopez|first=Stephanie|date=April 15, 2000|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|via=Google Books|archive-date=March 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250305185557/https://books.google.com/books?id=4w4EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA27#v=onepage&q&f=false|url-status=live|volume=112|number=16|issn=0006-2510}}</ref> while production was helmed by Joe and Tony Nicholas, featuring additional credit from Timmy Allen. It also appeared on the [[The Wood (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to the film ''[[The Wood]]'' (1999). Released as the lead single on November 7, 1999, it reached number four on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and number two on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart. The song was ranked fourth on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100's 2000 year-end chart.

"I Wanna Know" is a song by American R&B singer Joe. It was written by Joe, Joylon Skinner and Michele Williams for his third studio album My Name Is Joe, which was released on April 18, 2000, while production was helmed by Joe and Tony Nicholas, featuring additional credit from Timmy Allen. It also appeared on the soundtrack to the film The Wood (1999). Released as the lead single on November 7, 1999, it reached number four on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number two on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart. The song was ranked fourth on the Billboard Hot 100's 2000 year-end chart.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
According to the song's co-producer Edwin "Tony" Nicholas, "I Wanna Know" was originally intended for Joe's previous 1997 album ''[[All That I Am (Joe album)|All That I Am]]''. He removed the song from the final track listing due to taking issue with the [[Jive Records]] label heads wanting to be involved in the creative process. A few years later, he was asked to contribute a song to the [[The Wood (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] of the 1999 film ''[[The Wood]]'' and claimed he didn't have anything to send to the record label. He then sent in "I Wanna Know" because it happened to be lying around the studio. The song was then included on the 2000 album ''[[My Name Is Joe (album)|My Name is Joe]]'' and released as a single.<ref>{{cite web|title=YouKnowIGotSoul Interview With Producer Edwin "Tony" Nicholas|url=http://youknowigotsoul.com/youknowigotsoul-interview-with-producer-edwin-tony-nicholas|website=youknowigotsoul.com|publisher=You Know I Got Soul|access-date=June 23, 2015}}</ref>

A special remix of the song, entitled "The Roni Remix", can be found on a special U.K. edition of the 2001 album ''[[Better Days (Joe album)|Better Days]]'' as a bonus track. The remix retains most of the original version's lyrics but features a different instrumental from its original as well as additional lyrics. Another remix entitled "Phat Butt Remix" by Beau "DJ BO" van Gils is made in the 2Bro'z Boomroll Studios in [[Roermond]], The Netherlands, additional raps are also done by DJ BO. This remix is released on vinyl 12 inch and as bonustrack on the album.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video (directed by [[Bille Woodruff]]) starts out with a woman (played by [[Claudia Jordan]]) having an argument with her boyfriend in an alley off the street. Joe and two of his friends see the ongoing argument and after the woman's boyfriend leaves he approaches her and talks to her, in the process of obtaining her phone number. The rest of the music video shows Joe and the woman spending time with each other as their relationship becomes stronger. The woman is assumed to have cut off her relationship with her boyfriend from the beginning of the music video.
